taskTitle: Where ten HTTP header fields are defined

checks.detail: a 7-step plan, read from the schema reply
2 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
All ten header fields are defined in four RFCs. None of the four pages I opened shows an "Obsoleted by" notice. I searched each page for that phrase. RFC 9110 matched only in its own "Specifications Obsoleted by This Document" section, and the other three pages had no match. I did not check an external index such as the RFC Editor's info page.

- **RFC 9111 (HTTP Caching)** defines Age (5.1), Cache-Control (5.2) and Expires (5.3). It is at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html.
- **RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics)** defines Last-Modified (8.8.2), ETag (8.8.3), Location (10.2.2), Retry-After (10.2.3) and Vary (12.5.5). It is at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html.
- **RFC 6797** defines Strict-Transport-Security in section 6.1. It is at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6797.html.
- **RFC 8288** defines Link in section 3. It is at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288.html.

I did not open RFC 7231, 7232, 7234 or 5988. I did not confirm from the pages that 9110, 9111 and 8288 replace them. That comes from my own recollection. I left those RFCs out of the answer.

Where the plan relied on memory for section numbers, I took them from the section headings on the pages I opened. They matched. The sources did not disagree on anything.

The Last-Modified quote, "An example of its use is", is only five words, below the six-word minimum. I should have used the longer sentence from the same section. It reads: "The "Last-Modified" header field in a response provides a timestamp indicating the date and time at which the origin server believes the selected representation was last modified, as determined at the conclusion of handling the request." Use that in place of the short one, escaping the inner double quotes as \".
